findings.problem: BatchWorkflow uses status: String plus independent lifecycle booleans (is_validated, is_sent) and optional sent_at_epoch_ms, allowing contradictory states such as status="sent" with is_sent=false, or status="pending" with is_sent=true.
findings.failure_mode: Any downstream logic that trusts a single field (e.g. checking is_sent) while ignoring status can proceed with a batch in a logically inconsistent state, causing duplicate sends, lost acknowledgements, or silent data loss.
findings.fix: Replace status: String and lifecycle booleans with a single enum typestate (e.g. enum BatchStatus { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }). Remove is_validated and is_sent. Make sent_at_epoch_ms a field on the Sent variant, not an Option on the struct.

findings.problem: No typestate state machine exists. The struct has no enforced transitions; any field can be set to any value from any other state.
findings.failure_mode: Code can transition a batch from Sent back to Draft, double-increment sent counters, or mark a batch as sent without validation. No compiler-level guard prevents invalid transitions.
findings.fix: Define an enum typestate with explicit variants for each lifecycle stage. Use a method or constructor that only accepts the previous valid state and returns the next. Encode sent_at_epoch_ms inside the Sent variant rather than as a separate Option field.

findings.problem: id: String is a primitive string with no domain constraints. There is no newtype for batch identifiers.
findings.failure_mode: Any string (empty, random, malformed) is accepted as a batch ID. Cannot enforce format rules, uniqueness, or domain invariants at the type level.
findings.fix: Define a BatchId newtype (e.g. pub struct BatchId(String) or pub struct BatchId([u8; N])) with a fallible constructor that validates format. Use BatchId instead of String in BatchWorkflow.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs imperative mutation (to_string, field assignment) instead of a pure state transition. No validated pre-state is required.
findings.failure_mode: Any code can call mark_sent on a batch regardless of its current state, bypassing validation. The function has no pure core that computes the next state from the current state deterministically.
findings.fix: If using typestate, make mark_sent (or a method on the typestate) accept only the pre-sent state (e.g. BatchStatus::Validated) and return the post-sent state with an explicit timestamp. The transition logic itself should be a pure function with no allocations.

findings.problem: mark_sent allocates a new String via "sent".to_string() to set the status, even though the string literal is a compile-time constant.
findings.failure_mode: Every call to mark_sent performs a heap allocation for the same constant string. Under high throughput this adds unnecessary GC pressure and latency variance.
findings.fix: With the typestate refactoring, the Sent variant carries no String for status. If status must be stored, use an enum with no heap allocation. If keeping the current struct, assign a static reference or an enum discriminant instead of to_string().

findings.problem: The struct allows is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None, meaning a batch is marked sent but has no timestamp recording when it was sent.
findings.failure_mode: Audit trails are incomplete. Time-based queries, SLA tracking, and replay logic will fail silently for batches where is_sent=true but sent_at_epoch_ms=None.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of an enum typestate so it is impossible to be in the Sent state without a timestamp. The type system enforces presence.

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The primary risk is that the struct permits logically contradictory batch states with no compiler-level enforcement. The typestate + enum refactoring eliminates this risk class entirely.
